study.question: Does a constant-period approximation predict the same held-out observations as an amplitude-sensitive alternative?
study.measurement_protocol: FICTIONAL teaching fixture: predeclare fixed-length pendulum periods for three launch angles. In real experiments, control length, gravity, friction and timing error, use blinded repeated trials and independent instruments.

models.label: Small-angle constant-period approximation
models.hypothesis: The period is nearly constant across the tested range.

models.label: Amplitude-dependent alternative
models.hypothesis: The period changes with larger initial angles.

targets.condition: FICTIONAL controlled pendulum, 1 m length, 5-degree initial angle
FICTIONAL controlled pendulum, 1 m length, 40-degree initial angle
FICTIONAL controlled pendulum, 1 m length, 70-degree initial angle
